description: Rhizopus stolonifer is a common fungus that causes soft rot in many fruits and vegetables, especially after harvest. It grows rapidly in warm and humid conditions and spreads easily through airborne spores. The disease mainly attacks ripe or wounded produce with high sugar content.
symptoms: Soft watery rot on fruits or vegetables
Rapid tissue breakdown and leakage of juice
White cotton-like fungal growth on the surface
Development of black sporangia (black mold dots)
Sour or acidic smell from infected produce
Rapid decay spreading to nearby fruits
favorable_conditions: High sugar content in ripe fruits
spread: Contact between infected and healthy fruits
management: Handle fruits carefully to avoid wounds
Remove and destroy infected fruits quickly
Maintain good hygiene in storage areas
biological_control: Fengycin-producing bacteria that inhibit fungal growth
prevention: Harvest fruits carefully to avoid injuries
Keep storage areas clean and disinfected
Avoid stacking damaged produce with healthy fruits
Reduce humidity during storage and transport
source: Bautista-Baños et al., Postharvest Decay of Fruits and Vegetables
Scientific literature on post-harvest fungal diseases
